title: Error: unable to lock database (db.lck exists)
summary: pacman creates a lock file while it works so that two package operations never change the database at the same time. If pacman was interrupted, the lock file stays behind and every later command fails with this error. Check that no pacman is running, then remove the leftover file.

aliases.text: failed to init transaction unable to lock database arch
how to delete db.lck arch linux
pacman lock file exists how to remove
pacman не может заблокировать базу данных

error_patterns: failed to init transaction (unable to lock database)
failed to synchronize all databases (unable to lock database)
could not lock database: File exists
prerequisites: Arch Linux or a distribution based on it (Manjaro, EndeavourOS) that uses pacman
Know that no software installation or update was running when the error appeared

steps.explain: Check whether a pacman process is still running. If nothing is printed (exit status 1 means no match), the lock is stale. If a process number is printed, wait for that operation to finish and do not delete the lock.
steps.expect: Nothing is printed. The command returns exit status 1, which means no pacman process is running.

steps.explain: Confirm that the lock file exists. A 0-byte file named db.lck is the pacman lock. Step 1 decides whether it is safe to remove it.
steps.expect: -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 ... /var/lib/pacman/db.lck. If you see 'No such file or directory', the lock is already gone and the error has another cause.

steps.explain: Delete the stale lock file. Run this only when step 1 printed nothing. Then run the pacman command that failed again.
steps.expect: No output. The command finishes silently.

alternatives.explain: Use this if sudo is not installed. A fresh Arch Linux install has no sudo, so use su to become root. It asks for the root password.
alternatives.expect: No output after you enter the root password.

verify.expect: ls: cannot access '/var/lib/pacman/db.lck': No such file or directory

rollback.explain: Nothing to undo. pacman creates the lock file again the next time it runs, so no command is needed to restore it.

warnings: Never delete the lock while pacman, an AUR helper (yay, paru) or a graphical package tool (Pamac) is running. Two package operations at once can corrupt the package database.
If the lock was left behind by an interrupted upgrade, the system can be in a partly updated state. Run a full upgrade again with sudo pacman -Syu after removing the lock.
